# Frame TV Art Manager

> Frame TV Art Manager is a self-hosted service that keeps the art on one or more Samsung Frame TVs (The Frame) in sync with a folder of JPEG and PNG images on a NAS or home server. It prepares each picture for the TV's 3840x2160 screen, uploads it over the local network, and rotates art automatically when the TV's storage is full. No Samsung or SmartThings account is needed.

Last substantive update: 2026-10-24
Maintainer: MikeO7 (https://github.com/MikeO7)
Website: https://mikeo7.github.io/frame-tv-art-manager/
Source: https://github.com/MikeO7/frame-tv-art-manager

## Key facts

- Who it is for: Samsung Frame TV owners who run an always-on NAS, Unraid server, mini PC, Raspberry Pi-class Linux board, or Mac.
- Supported TVs: Samsung Frame TVs running Tizen 8.0 or newer. Other firmware may work, but Samsung's private Art Mode protocol varies between models and releases.
- Install: Docker image ghcr.io/mikeo7/frame-tv-art-manager:latest (amd64, arm64, armv7), or build a single Go binary.
- Only required setting: TV_IPS, a comma-separated list of TV IP addresses. Several TVs are supported.
- Storage: a persistent /data volume. Art lives in /data/artwork; pairing tokens and per-TV state live in /data/tokens (saved with 0600 permissions).
- Pairing: on first connection the TV shows an Allow/Deny prompt named by CLIENT_NAME (default "Frame Art Manager"). Approve once.
- Schedule: first sync at startup, then every SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES (default 30).
- Connection: talks directly to the TV on the local network. A folder-only setup needs no SmartThings, Samsung account, or cloud service.

## Adding art

- Local folder of JPEG and PNG files (.jpg, .jpeg, .png). Exact duplicates are detected by file contents.
- Optional web uploader: UPLOAD_ENABLED=true; HTTP Basic auth with username "frame" and password UPLOAD_TOKEN (at least 16 characters); GET or POST /upload on port 8080; form field "file"; size limit MAX_DOWNLOAD_SIZE_MB (default 20). Works from a browser, iOS Shortcuts, and curl. Keep it on a trusted network.
- Optional sources file (ARTWORK_SOURCES_FILE): Unsplash, NASA (APOD and search), Art Institute of Chicago, Pexels, Pixabay, and direct image URLs.

## Image preparation (on by default)

- EXIF orientation, portrait handling (PORTRAIT_MODE: crop by default, pad, or collage), resize to exactly 3840x2160 (configurable with IMAGE_MAX_WIDTH and IMAGE_MAX_HEIGHT), color-profile conversion to sRGB, HDR PNG tone mapping, light sharpening, JPEG quality 95.
- The prepared version replaces the original file in the artwork folder, so users should copy pictures in and keep originals elsewhere.
- Memory budget per picture: IMAGE_MAX_WORKING_MEMORY_MB (default 512). A 24-megapixel photo takes about 1-2 seconds and about 250 MiB. 8K photos fit.
- Optional and off by default: smart (saliency) crop, an external HTTP crop service, and a "museum mode" canvas and warmth effect.
- Samsung mattes: MATTE_STYLE (default none, for example shadowbox_polar), with per-file overrides in mattes.json.

## Full TVs and rotation

- The manager learns a TV's capacity the first time the TV rejects an upload because storage is full. It does not estimate or probe.
- If the collection is larger than the TV holds, each piece the manager uploaded stays at least ROTATION_INTERVAL_DAYS (default 14; fractions allowed; 0 disables), then is swapped for waiting art: never-shown pieces first, then the pieces away longest.
- Rotated-out art does not return until it has been away for the same interval, so large collections cycle fully.
- Each swap is one delete followed immediately by one upload; the TV is never more than one piece short.
- Only art the manager uploaded is rotated. Art added another way is never touched. Local files are never deleted by rotation.
- /status shows rotating, artwork_waiting, and next_rotation for each TV.
- If uploads keep failing after space was freed (TVs that limit by size rather than count), rotation pauses after 3 such failures until an upload succeeds.
- With rotation off, a full TV reports "storage full", keeps its existing art, and retries one upload every 24 hours.

## Safety rules

- Never deletes TV art it did not upload unless REMOVE_UNKNOWN_IMAGES=true.
- Does not choose which artwork is displayed. If the piece on screen is removed or rotated out, the TV shows another piece.
- Keeps the last piece it uploaded if the folder becomes empty.
- A failed source download never deletes previously downloaded art.
- Makes no changes to a TV whose state it cannot confirm.
- DRY_RUN=true reads and plans without uploading, deleting, saving state, or waking the TV. It needs an existing pairing.

## Optional TV controls

- Slideshow: SLIDESHOW_ENABLED, SLIDESHOW_INTERVAL (3, 15, 60, 720, or 1440 minutes), SLIDESHOW_TYPE (shuffle or sequential). Untouched unless set.
- Brightness: fixed with BRIGHTNESS (0-50), or following the sun with SOLAR_BRIGHTNESS_ENABLED plus latitude, longitude, and timezone.
- Nightly power-off for TVs in Art Mode: AUTO_OFF_TIME.
- Wake-on-LAN: TV_MAC, sent only when the TV is known to be off; single TV only.

## Monitoring

- GET /live, /ready, /health, and /status on HEALTH_PORT (default 8080). /ready and /health return 200 after a successful sync.
- Logs are structured JSON.

## Common questions

- Does it need a Samsung account? No, not for a local folder.
- Will it delete art I added myself? No, unless REMOVE_UNKNOWN_IMAGES=true.
- What happens when the TV is full? It rotates the art it uploaded, 14 days per piece by default.
- Does it pick what is on screen? No. The TV and its slideshow decide.
- Can it manage several TVs? Yes, list them in TV_IPS.
- What does it run on? Docker on amd64, arm64, or armv7, or a Go binary on Linux or macOS.
- Is it open source? No. It is source-available under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 and free for noncommercial use.
- When is SmartThings better? For occasional manual uploads from a phone without a home server.
